brief.subject: FTC sues alleged passport impersonators; debt scheme shut down
brief.headline: FTC Targets Passport-Service Impersonators and Shuts Down Debt Relief Scheme
brief.dek: Regulators act against operations posing as the government to sell passport help and debt relief to seniors and veterans.
brief.lede: The FTC is suing companies it says posed as the federal government to sell passport services through paid search ads. If you need a passport, be wary of ads that look official.

sections.heading: Fake 'government' passport help
bullets: The FTC sued GovAssist LLC, Entry LLC and Scott Zuckerman over an alleged government impersonation scheme.
The operation allegedly targeted people seeking passport services by claiming to be, or be tied to, the federal government.
Paid search ads were allegedly used to mislead, so the top result is not always the official agency.
The FTC also cites misleading promises and fake reviews, so glowing ratings alone don't prove a service is legitimate.

sections.heading: Debt relief scheme permanently banned
bullets: A federal court permanently banned operators of an alleged debt relief scheme, at the FTC's request.
The scheme allegedly targeted seniors and veterans by posing as banks, card companies and government agencies.
On October 14, 2026, the court entered a $106.8 million default judgment against the corporate defendants.
Unsolicited debt-help offers that claim to come from your bank or an agency deserve extra scrutiny.

sections.heading: FTC reports on fraud against older adults
bullets: The FTC sent Congress its report, Protecting Older Consumers 2025-2026.
It draws on fraud reports filed by older adults to highlight key scam trends.
It also outlines enforcement actions aimed at deceptive practices hurting older Americans, useful context for families watching out for parents.

brief.seo_description: FTC sues alleged passport-service impersonators, court bans debt relief scheme targeting seniors, and FTC reports on fraud against older adults.
